guides.vulnerability_name: Windows DNS Server Remote Code Execution
guides.treatment_action:
Recommended treatment actions:  
- Implement and enforce multi-factor authentication for all remote access to SRV-02, SRV-03, and SRV-04  
- Apply the latest security patches to address CVE-2020-1350, CVE-2017-0144, and CVE-2021-31166 on affected hosts  
- Configure network access control to restrict remote connections to only authorized IP ranges and ports  
- Conduct regular vulnerability scans and penetration tests to identify and remediate unpatched systems
guides.evidence_name: Evidence for SRV-02 under control 6.7 demonstrates that multi-factor authenti...
guides.evidence_description: Evidence for SRV-02 under control 6.7 demonstrates that multi-factor authentication is enforced for remote access, ensuring secure remote working practices and mitigating risks from unpatched vulnerabilities like CVE-2020-1350.

references.source: Microsoft Security Response Center guidance for CVE-2020-1350
Microsoft Security Compliance Toolkit / Windows Security Baselines

implementation_steps.title: Confirm DNS Service Exposure
implementation_steps.description: Confirm that SRV-02 is operating the Windows DNS Server role and identify DNS listener exposure before applying the treatment for Windows DNS Server Remote Code Execution (CVE-2020-1350).
implementation_steps.expected_result: DNS service status, TCP/UDP 53 listeners, and DNS diagnostic configuration are captured for SRV-02.
implementation_steps.output_type: DNS service status / listener list / DNS diagnostics
implementation_steps.evidence_capture: Save the DNS service output, port 53 listener output, and DNS diagnostics from SRV-02.

implementation_steps.title: Validate DNS Server Security Updates
implementation_steps.description: Check whether SRV-02 has the Windows security updates required to remediate Windows DNS Server Remote Code Execution (CVE-2020-1350); patch the server through the approved maintenance process if gaps remain.
implementation_steps.expected_result: Patch state for SRV-02 is known and missing DNS Server security updates are identified or installed.
implementation_steps.output_type: Patch inventory / update scan output
implementation_steps.evidence_capture: Capture installed hotfix output and the update scan or change ticket showing DNS Server patch status.

implementation_steps.title: Apply DNS-Specific Mitigation
implementation_steps.description: If the approved treatment requires interim mitigation for Windows DNS Server Remote Code Execution, apply the DNS Server packet-size mitigation and restart DNS during the approved change window.
implementation_steps.expected_result: The DNS mitigation value is present on SRV-02 and DNS service is restarted successfully.
implementation_steps.output_type: Registry value / service restart output
implementation_steps.evidence_capture: Capture the registry query result and DNS service restart output for SRV-02.

implementation_steps.title: Restrict DNS Network Access
implementation_steps.description: Restrict DNS traffic to approved resolver/client networks so SRV-02 is not broadly exposed while supporting required DNS operations.
commands: New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "Allow DNS from approved subnets" -Direction Inbound -Protocol UDP -LocalPort 53 -Action Allow
implementation_steps.expected_result: DNS firewall rules are reviewed and restricted to the approved network path for SRV-02.
implementation_steps.output_type: Firewall rule list / firewall change record
implementation_steps.evidence_capture: Export firewall rule evidence showing allowed DNS paths for SRV-02.

implementation_steps.title: Verify DNS Resolution And Logs
implementation_steps.description: Validate that DNS service still resolves expected names after remediation and review DNS events for errors.
implementation_steps.expected_result: DNS resolution works, DNS service remains running, and no new critical DNS errors are observed.
implementation_steps.output_type: DNS query output / DNS event log excerpt / service status
implementation_steps.evidence_capture: Capture DNS query results, DNS event log excerpts, and final DNS service status for SRV-02.

guides.treatment_action:
Recommended treatment actions:  
- Apply the latest security patches to address CVE-2020-1472 and CVE-2020-1350 on SRV-01  
- Implement network segmentation to isolate SRV-01 from other network segments  
- Configure firewall rules to restrict unnecessary inbound and outbound traffic to SRV-01  
- Enable and enforce least privilege access controls for administrative accounts on SRV-01
guides.evidence_name: Evidence that network segmentation, firewall rule restrictions, and applied s...
guides.evidence_description: Evidence that network segmentation, firewall rule restrictions, and applied security patches have been implemented on SRV-01 to mitigate the Netlogon Elevation of Privilege vulnerability and secure network access under control 8.2.

references.source: Microsoft Security Response Center guidance for CVE-2020-1472
Microsoft Security Compliance Toolkit / Windows Security Baselines

implementation_steps.title: Confirm Domain Controller Role And Secure Channel Scope
implementation_steps.description: Confirm SRV-01 is a domain controller and identify Netlogon secure channel exposure before applying treatment for Netlogon Elevation of Privilege (CVE-2020-1472).
implementation_steps.expected_result: Domain controller identity, Netlogon service status, and domain secure channel context are captured.
implementation_steps.output_type: Domain controller details / Netlogon service status
implementation_steps.evidence_capture: Save the domain controller query output and Netlogon service status from SRV-01.

implementation_steps.title: Validate Netlogon Remediation Patch State
implementation_steps.description: Verify that SRV-01 has the Windows Server security updates required for Netlogon Elevation of Privilege (CVE-2020-1472); remediate through the domain controller patch process if needed.
implementation_steps.expected_result: Patch evidence confirms whether SRV-01 has the required Netlogon remediation updates.
implementation_steps.output_type: Patch inventory / update scan output
implementation_steps.evidence_capture: Capture hotfix inventory and update/change ticket evidence for the domain controller patch.

implementation_steps.title: Enforce Secure Netlogon Behavior
implementation_steps.description: Apply or verify secure Netlogon enforcement on SRV-01 so vulnerable secure channel behavior is blocked.
implementation_steps.expected_result: Secure Netlogon enforcement is configured and Netlogon restarts successfully on SRV-01.
implementation_steps.output_type: Registry value / Netlogon service restart output
implementation_steps.evidence_capture: Capture the Netlogon registry value and service restart output for SRV-01.

implementation_steps.title: Review Netlogon Enforcement Events
implementation_steps.description: Review Netlogon-related events on SRV-01 to identify denied or non-compliant secure channel activity.
implementation_steps.expected_result: Netlogon enforcement events are reviewed and any non-compliant clients are identified for follow-up.
implementation_steps.output_type: System event log excerpt / security event log excerpt
implementation_steps.evidence_capture: Export Netlogon enforcement events and related security log excerpts from SRV-01.

implementation_steps.title: Validate Domain Authentication Health
implementation_steps.description: Confirm domain authentication and replication remain healthy after Netlogon hardening on SRV-01.
implementation_steps.expected_result: Domain controller checks pass and secure channel validation succeeds after treatment.
implementation_steps.output_type: DCDIAG output / replication summary / secure channel validation
implementation_steps.evidence_capture: Capture DCDIAG, replication, and secure channel validation output for SRV-01.

guides.evidence_name: The host SRV-02, acting as a DNS Server, is not configured for remote access,...
guides.evidence_description: The host SRV-02, acting as a DNS Server, is not configured for remote access, ensuring that its role does not introduce risks associated with remote working under control 6.7, thereby proving that security measures are in place to prevent exploitation of the identified vulnerability.
